speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where in your neck and arm the pain is located, and does it radiate down to your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness or numbness follow a specific pattern, such as affecting just the thumb and index finger or the pinky side of the hand, and have you noticed any loss of grip strength or difficulty with fine motor tasks? I need to determine if this is a single nerve root issue or a more complex peripheral neuropathy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of absent reflexes, fasciculations, and weakness suggests lower motor neuron involvement, which is concerning for a motor neuron disease rather than simple radiculopathy. REQUEST TEST: EMG_and_Nerve_Conduction_Studies. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cervical_Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Cervical_Spine: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region. EMG_and_Nerve_Conduction_Studies: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI reveals a syrinx, which explains your symptoms, but the normal EMG rules out motor neuron disease like ALS. This clinical picture of a cervical syrinx following trauma is highly suggestive of syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
